supported: Exact sequence matches the human xenin entry in GPCRdb; the original paper isolated xenin from human gastric mucosa and studied pancreatic secretion.
not_established: Whether the retained GHXTox positive label is erroneous; hormone identity neither establishes safety nor rules out dose-dependent toxicity
implication: Prioritize original-label evidence recovery rather than automatically fitting a correction to force a positive prediction.

supported: ConoServer reports exact sequence, venom source Conus betulinus, protein-level sequence evidence, and C-terminal amidation. Original paper identified NPY-like conopeptides.
not_established: A specific experimentally verified receptor, an assay-specific toxic threshold, provenance of the GHXTox binary label
implication: No-Cys venom peptide is a biologically plausible exception to a cysteine-rich toxin shortcut. Standard one-letter input omits documented amidation. Identity alone does not assign a receptor mechanism.

supported: Exact sequence appears in Hemolytik2 with species-dependent hemolytic measurements and PMID 18752624. Original paper studies synergistic hemolysins.
not_established: Original GHXTox label accession, whether a particular assay/condition determined its label, precise mechanism for this sequence in the GHXTox setting
implication: Low-Cys false negative with independently recorded hemolytic activity; prioritize retrieval of original assay and concentration. Do not infer that all low-Cys errors share this endpoint.
